proposal.utterance: Classify 'a property status' in BFO terms.

entities.label: PropertyStatus
entities.rationale: A 'property status' (e.g., owner, tenant, lessee, encumbered property holder) is an externally grounded social-legal position that a continuant bears in virtue of recognition by a legal system or social practice. It is not internally grounded (ruling out Disposition) and is not a static measurable magnitude (ruling out Quality). It is paradigmatically a Role: it inheres in a bearer (a person or a material entity such as land) and is conferred by external relational facts (legal title, registration, recognition). BFO_0000023 (Role) is the best fit. This is a common noun denoting a kind, so it is a class, not an individual.

relations.rationale: PropertyStatus is a subclass of Role (BFO_0000023) because property statuses are externally grounded specifically dependent continuants that inhere in bearers (persons or material entities) and are realizable in legal or social processes.

open_questions: Should 'property status' apply only to persons (e.g., the role of 'owner' inhering in a person), or also to material entities (e.g., land bearing the status of 'encumbered property')? This affects whether the domain of RO_0000052 (inheres in) points to BFO_0000040 persons, BFO_0000040 land parcels, or both.
Is there a specific property status (e.g., 'Owner', 'Lessee', 'Mortgagor') you want to model as a subclass of PropertyStatus, or is the general class sufficient for now?
Should PropertyStatus be further related to existing working classes such as LegalRight or LegalObligation (e.g., bearing a PropertyStatus typically entails bearing certain LegalRights)?
proposal.rationale_summary: A 'property status' denotes a kind of socially and legally conferred position that a continuant bears in virtue of external recognition — the hallmark of BFO Role (BFO_0000023). Unlike a Quality, it is not a measurable intrinsic magnitude; unlike a Disposition, it is not grounded in the internal constitution of the bearer but in relational legal facts (title registration, deed, court recognition). The class PropertyStatus is therefore proposed as a subclass of BFO_0000023 (Role). It is typed as a class because 'a property status' is a common noun denoting a kind, not a named individual. No existing working class directly captures this concept (LegalRight and LegalObligation are already roles but are narrower), so a new class is minted. Open questions concern the domain of the inheres-in relation and possible subclassing for specific statuses such as Owner or Lessee.
